prompt:
Write the appraiser's remarks (about 80 words) on a body shop repair estimate after a hit while turning left. Describe the damage seen on the vehicle and the repair plan. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1412; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
- The repair labor hours are a little high for this damage.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
text: The rear quarter panel and bumper cover on the vehicle show damage consistent with the impact described, with the crease and paint transfer lining up with a left-turn collision. Parts and labor are itemized, and the billing reflects no repeated charges. The labor hours run a little high for this scope of damage, so the shop should justify the time on the body work. No prior damage to this vehicle is known. The repair plan is to replace the bumper cover, repair and refinish the quarter panel, and recalibrate the rear sensor. Approval is recommended once the labor figures are reviewed.
